label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never D1/GO), and almost only when this trial chose a1 (99% of mass). Strongest, near-max activations (~0.8-1.0 of max) when a1 led to S2, i.e. the rare transition for a1; this conjunction (directly observed inputs at D2: last action a1, state S2) gives dev P=0.93, R=0.74, mass recall 0.93. The remaining recall misses are weak activations (~0.05-0.3 of max) on a1->S1 common D2 steps; a2 trials (either state) are essentially silent. Not modulated by the previous reward. Rate is higher late in episodes and when value is low, a correlate of the S2-after-a1 events.

issues: The main claims check out on test. The predicate scores P=0.927, R=0.744, F1=0.825, mass recall 0.933. 'phase != D2' has zero recall, so the unit really is D2-only. D2&a2 has recall 0.027 and mass 0.00007, so a2 trials really are near-silent. Previous reward does not modulate it: on a1->S2 the precision is 0.938 with prev_reward=0 and 0.922 with prev_reward=1.

The misses are not scattered noise but one systematic class: weak firing at D2 after a1->S1 (common), and only late in the episode. On test, D2&a1&S1 gives P=0.10, R=0.235, mass 0.06. With ep_bucket<=3 that predicate gets P=0 and R=0. Restricting to ep_trial>=60 keeps the full 0.235 recall (P=0.26); ep_trial>=80 gives P=0.49, R=0.21; ep_trial>=90 gives P=0.61. So almost all of these a1->S1 activations come from trials 60 and later, rising toward the end of the episode.

This refutes the explanation's claim that the late-episode / low-value effect 'correlates with how often a1->S2 happens rather than reflecting a separate pattern'. The late-episode drift is exactly the separate pattern behind the missed recall. Low value also tracks it: D2&a1&S1 with value in the bottom 20% gives P=0.51.
A smaller related effect: a1->S2 at D2 is mostly silent very early in the episode (ep_bucket<=2: P=0.32, though the count is tiny).

Better predicate on test: (phase==D2)&(in_action==1)&((in_state==2)|(ep_trial>=90)) gives P=0.865, R=0.865, F1=0.865, mass 0.972, against 0.825 for the original. ep_trial is not a model input, but the agent can track elapsed time in its hidden state; no FUTURE variable is used.
